body.hook: Does listening to music while studying help or hurt? Your friends might swear by it, but psychologists don't settle questions with opinions. They design experiments where only one thing changes at a time.

study.title: Design an Experiment
study.question: How do psychologists design fair experiments?
study.passage:
Research question: Does background music affect memory?
Step 1, Variables: IV = music (lyrics, instrumental, silence). DV = number of words recalled from a list of 20 after 2 minutes.
Step 2, Hypothesis (if-then-because): "If students study with music with lyrics, then they will recall fewer words than students studying in silence, because lyrics compete for language processing."
Step 3, Operational definitions: "Music with lyrics" = a chosen pop song at 60 dB; "recall" = words correctly written in 2 minutes.
Step 4, Controls: same word list, same room, same time of day, same instructions, same volume.
Step 5, Random assignment: draw names from a hat for each condition.
Step 6, Confounds: prior knowledge of the words, fatigue, whether students know the song. How will you reduce them?
Step 7, Ethics: informed consent, right to withdraw, no harm, confidentiality, debriefing.
Task: In groups, design an experiment for one question: Does sleep affect reaction time? Do colours affect mood? Does chewing gum improve concentration? Complete all seven steps.
